topStories.headline: West Portal Elementary Turns 100 — and Two New Buildings to Prove It
topStories.dek: Phase 1 of the bond-funded modernization project opened for students at the start of the 2026–27 school year, replacing eight aging bungalows; a centennial street celebration follows this Saturday.
topStories.body:
West Portal Elementary School opened its doors in 1926, and a century later the campus looks measurably different. Phase 1 of the SFUSD modernization project — a $21 million effort funded in part by state bond reimbursements — removed eight dilapidated portable bungalows and replaced them with two new permanent buildings. According to SFUSD's project page, the new structures welcomed students at the start of the 2026–27 school year, with a Phase 1 ribbon-cutting marking the milestone. A second package of work, focused on modernizing the main building, began during the summer of 2026.

The school was initially constructed between 1926 and 1927, making this academic year its centennial. Construction had been delayed for years due to insufficient funds before SFUSD received state bond reimbursements and restarted work in early 2024. The project was designed by WRNS Studio, managed by Kitchell, and built by Bana Builders.

The Greater West Portal Neighborhood Association is marking the occasion with a public celebration on West Portal Avenue this Saturday, October 3, from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m., starting at the West Portal Library courtyard. The West Portal Parents Club describes the centennial as "a celebration of the families, educators, and community members who have shaped the school for the last 100 years — and those who will carry it forward into the next century."

topStories.headline: SFSU's First Woman President to Step Down Next Summer
topStories.dek: Lynn Mahoney announced September 8 that she will retire after eight years leading San Francisco State University, as new student enrollment hits a record high under her tenure.
topStories.body:
San Francisco State University President Lynn Mahoney announced on September 8, 2026, that she will retire next summer after eight years as president and nearly two decades of service to the California State University system. Mahoney, who in 2019 became the first woman to serve as SFSU's president in a permanent capacity, will remain in her role while the CSU Board of Trustees conducts a national search for her successor.

Mahoney's tenure was marked by steep enrollment losses, budget cuts, and a challenging pandemic period — but also signs of a rebound. This fall, new student enrollment at SFSU increased by more than 10 percent, a first under her leadership. During her time at the helm, the university opened the Science and Engineering Innovation Center, Marcus Hall, and two new residence halls, including West Grove Commons. The university also raised $175.8 million in philanthropic support and earned the Seal of Excelencia for its work serving Latinx students.

Campus reaction was mixed. The student newspaper Golden Gate Xpress reported that while some praised Mahoney's legacy — particularly the university's divestment from weapons manufacturers — others raised unresolved concerns about staff and faculty conditions. CSU Chancellor Mildred García praised Mahoney's "candid, respectful, and authentic two-way engagement" with the campus community in a public statement.

topStories.headline: West Portal Safety Overhaul Is Working, SFMTA Data Shows
topStories.dek: An SFMTA evaluation published in mid-2026 found that injury crashes in the West Portal station area dropped 60 percent since traffic changes were implemented following the 2024 fatal crash.
topStories.body:
Two years after a car plowed into a bus shelter at West Portal Station and killed a family of four, city data shows the neighborhood's safety overhaul is producing results. The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency completed an evaluation of the West Portal Station Safety and Community Space Improvements project and published results in its June 2026 report, with findings highlighted by the Metropolitan Transportation Commission in August.

According to SFMTA, traffic collision rates in the area dropped 60 percent between October 2024 and March 2026 compared to the same window before the project. The number of injury crashes fell from an average of 6.7 per year to 2.7 per year. Crashes involving Muni vehicles also declined sharply — as of fall 2025, no Muni vehicle had been involved in a collision with another vehicle in the project area. More than 70 percent of people surveyed reported feeling very or somewhat safe at the intersection, up from about 50 percent before the project.

The improvements — approved by the SFMTA board in mid-2024 and implemented in phases through 2025 — included turn restrictions on Ulloa Street, a redesigned station entrance, station murals, decorative crosswalks, a bikeshare station, and flashing pedestrian beacons. SFMTA also noted that sales tax growth along the West Portal Avenue commercial corridor has exceeded the citywide average since the changes were made. The agency says it will consider additional permanent improvements based on the evaluation findings.

moreNews.headline: Miraloma Park Improvement Club Posts Notice of Election
moreNews.body: The Miraloma Park Improvement Club has posted a notice of election for officer and board member positions on its website, listed among current announcements alongside the September 2026 issue of its Miraloma Life newsletter. The club, which has governed neighborhood advocacy since 1930 and holds monthly meetings at its clubhouse on O'Shaughnessy Boulevard, has not yet published dates or candidate details on its public site. Members should check miralomapark.org for voting instructions and deadlines.

moreNews.headline: Parkmerced Development Parcels Pass to New York Firm After Foreclosure
moreNews.body: In late July 2026, New York-based Yellowstone Real Estate Investments took control of four land parcels at Parkmerced through foreclosure after originating a $101 million construction loan to developer Maximus Real Estate in 2022. The parcels cover the first four subphases of a long-delayed redevelopment plan and are entitled for nearly 1,700 new apartments. The broader Parkmerced complex — 3,221 existing units adjacent to San Francisco State University — remains under the management of court-appointed receiver Douglas Wilson Cos. and property manager Ballast. The redevelopment plan was approved by the city in 2011 and was originally slated to triple Parkmerced's housing stock to more than 5,600 units with new Muni M-line stops, but never broke ground. Whether and when Yellowstone will begin construction has not been announced.

moreNews.headline: SFSU Student Paper Reports Persistent Accessibility Gaps for Disabled Students
moreNews.body: A September 25 investigation by the Golden Gate Xpress, SFSU's student newspaper, found that the university's accessibility features for disabled students have shown "patterns of inconsistency despite promises of dedication." The story documented shuttle service failures, accommodation desks being used as ordinary tables, and communication breakdowns between students and the Disability Programs and Resource Center. The report comes as campus attention to disability issues has grown; the DPRC this fall shifted from drop-in hours to scheduled twice-weekly office hours with designated disability specialists, a change that took effect in January 2026.
